ten_year.rationale: The ten-year is 5.12 after the same backup, so paying it adds no separate trend and sits further from the policy path.

two_year.rationale: The US two-year at 4.83 has backed up with the dollar. Paying it rides the policy-linked yield trend directly.

expression_memo.rationale: Pay the US two-year rather than short NZDUSD. The two-year backup is the fresh rate impulse behind the dollar, while NZDUSD is already at a five-year low and the far SOFR contracts are not making new highs versus March.

spot_candidate.rationale: Short NZDUSD at 0.5515, a five-year low with a live 20-day downside break, is the cleanest spot continuation.

lifecycle.catalyst_logic: The edge exhausts if the 26 to 32 basis point backup is fully retraced or the hike path falls back toward SOFR cash at 3.90.
lifecycle.realization_logic: The short US two-year pays if the yield keeps rising with the five-day backup and the dollar uptrend.

trend-follower.invalidation: The two-year short is done if the five-day yield backup is fully retraced or the hike path falls back toward SOFR cash at 3.90. The yen long is done if spot trades back through the 159.23 entry.
trend-follower.thesis: Hold the 10 million USDJPY long and open a 15 million short in the US two-year. Dollar strength and the yield backup are still the trends in force: the two-year is 4.83 and the ten-year is 5.12 after a 26 to 32 basis point rise in five days, and the growth currencies are breaking down. The yen long stays a ride because spot at 159.60 is above the 159.23 entry. The failed 20-day upside break blocks an add and is not a trend reversal.

expression_memo.rationale: Euro-sterling at 0.8345 is unchanged on the week and still a one-year extreme against the 0.8343 entry. The US ten-year, kiwi, euro-dollar, and dollar-Canada are five-year extremes that are still breaking.

value-guy.invalidation: The euro long is invalidated if euro-sterling stays pinned near 0.834 after euro-dollar and euro-yen have lifted off their lows, or if a renewed rise in crude marks that cheapness as fair.
value-guy.thesis: Hold the five million euro-sterling long. At 0.8345 the cross is almost unchanged on the week, still a one-year z-score near minus 2.5 and about the 9th percentile of five years, so the discount versus sterling has not closed. Convergence is a drift back toward the middle of that one-year range. The US ten-year and the still-breaking dollar extremes are poorer fades because those trends have not failed.

expression_memo.rationale: A bounded option is the preferred expression because oil can gap on Hormuz headlines or the export-recovery note, and the 10-year backup can extend or reverse. No listed premium, strike, or implied volatility is quoted, so the option cannot be priced. Spot and a rates receive do not bound that gap.

vol-convexity.invalidation: The flat stance ends if a listed premium and strike are quoted and that premium is cheap relative to the two-way Hormuz headlines and the backup already in the 10-year at 5.12.
vol-convexity.thesis: Hold flat, with no option structure and no size. Euro at 1.1014 has broken the 20-day low, dollar-yen at 159.60 has failed a 20-day upside break, the US 10-year is 5.12 after a 26 basis point backup, and Brent at 92.44 sits between Hormuz headlines and a same-day export-recovery note. That mix is two-way event risk, so the right instrument is a bounded option, and no listed premium, strike, or implied volatility is quoted to price one.
